column3: Measured years of suspended dwelling supply a time-counting parallel, without the focus's enjoyment and reckoning.
The scale of a divine day corrects impatience for punishment and frames years of delay within an unfailing promise.
Enjoyment joined to ingratitude and later knowledge supports the focus's warning that present use postpones rather than cancels disclosure.
Counting years spent on earth from the final horizon directly tests whether a long earthly span had lasting weight.
The immediate local refusal to believe until painful punishment locates the extended enjoyment within persistent disbelief.
Provision for people and livestock identifies matāʿ as usable sustenance, though it does not itself state its limit.
Years of residence become a disputed human measure, offering a local temporal parallel without the focus's granted enjoyment.
The local question about being granted respite turns the focus's hypothetical extension into the hearers' request for more delay.
Good enjoyment is explicitly bounded by an appointed term and set beside the prospect of a great day's punishment.
The interrogative formula is shared, but this turning-away scene adds no account of years or prolonged benefit.
The selected appointment after years supplies only a remote temporal resonance with the focus's extended interval.
Noah's exceptionally long stay ends in punishment of persistent wrongdoers, showing that length of time is not acquittal.
The rhetorical question about idols shares wording but adds nothing about delay, enjoyment, or promised consequence.
The local warning that punishment arrives suddenly supplies the counterpoint to the years posited in the focus.
Even wishing for a thousand-year life cannot move one away from punishment, directly limiting the value of prolonged life.
The challenge to an unbeliever's claim of wealth and children has only a loose rhetorical resemblance to the focus.
The promise eventually coming to them is the immediate completion of the focus's conditional question.
Thamud are told to enjoy themselves only until a time, making the reprieve explicitly finite before their destruction.
The formula introduces a case of desire as god, but its concern is moral blindness rather than extended enjoyment.
The local question about hastening punishment exposes the impatience that misreads the years imagined in the focus.
Brief enjoyment is addressed to the guilty and paired with their guilt, sharply denying that use implies safety.
A precisely stated long residence adds counted duration, but its cave setting does not develop enjoyment or consequence.
The local conclusion explicitly says that what they had been allowed to enjoy did not avail them.
The command to enjoy is followed by future knowing, casting present benefit as a limited interval before disclosure.
A few years under divine command show that temporal intervals are ordered, though no enjoyment or judgment is at issue.
The inhabitants' estimate of a day or part of one recasts experienced residence as small within a larger reckoning.
Repentance removes impending punishment and grants enjoyment until a time, showing that the extended interval is morally responsive rather than secure possession.
The required provision on divorce uses the same root in a legal setting but does not illuminate prolonged enjoyment.
The local insistence that destroyed towns had warners explains the justice surrounding the delayed arrival of punishment.
The prophet names possible enjoyment until a time as a test, directly treating delay as trial rather than vindication.
Flight cannot secure more than a little enjoyment before death, limiting the practical value of brief reprieve.
The divine verdict calls their residence only a little, sharpening the contrast between lived duration and final assessment.
Enjoyment of a people and their forebears lasts only until truth and a clear messenger arrive, exposing inherited comfort as delayed confrontation.
The provision offered in a divorce choice is unrelated to the focus's years of communal reprieve.
The local denial of injustice confirms that the eventual consequence after warning and delay is not arbitrary.
This duplicate provision-for-people-and-livestock formula adds little beyond the earlier identification of matāʿ as sustenance.
Showing off is unrelated to the focus's temporal extension and its eventual consequence.
The alternation of night and day makes years countable, giving a calendrical frame for the focus's measured years.
This later repetition of enjoyment followed by knowing adds little after the clearer earlier instance.
Mutual enjoyment reaches an externally appointed term and ends in the Fire, directly denying that sustained use is self-securing.
Years of waiting in Midian culminate in arrival at an appointed measure, a temporal pattern adjacent to the focus's controlled interval.
Long enjoyment and old age create an illusion of dominance while their domain is being reduced, directly challenging security inferred from duration.
Disbelievers' enjoyment and consumption are contrasted with their final dwelling, making worldly use non-final.
The call to worship and fear God supplies no distinct account of years, enjoyment, or deferred consequence.
Mercy and enjoyment are explicitly only until a time, though the verse gives no further account of the promised arrival.
Belief results in enjoyment until a time, providing a conditional counterpart to the focus's warning about prolonged benefit.
Defeat begins a scheduled reversal sequence but contributes little without the following verses' timeframe.
Enjoyment of generations until they forget the reminder shows how prolonged comfort can produce heedlessness rather than security.
The description of wandering in intoxication adds no temporal-benefit or deferred-punishment element.
The assurance that Allah does not fail His promise explains why delay cannot invalidate the outcome, though enjoyment is absent.
Enjoyment is called little before compulsion to severe punishment, directly condensing the focus's contrast between duration and outcome.
The shared question form and conditional introduce a guidance case, not prolonged enjoyment or its limit.
The divine Lord of the ascent gives only a broad link to a larger scale of time.
Eating, enjoyment, and distracting hope culminate in future knowing, closely describing the mechanism of heedless reprieve.
The assertion of power to restore fingertips has no material connection to enjoyment across years.
This intermediate defeat-to-victory line has only a remote relation to controlled temporal intervals.
Earthly settlement and enjoyment are expressly only until a time, furnishing a foundational finite-use pattern.
The command to turn away from opponents does not add to the focus's account of delay and benefit.
Divine aid in victory offers a broad providential setting but no enjoyment or duration judgment.
Worldly life is characterized as deceptive enjoyment whose visible flourishing withers, giving the focus a general account of false permanence.
Noah's public call does not itself clarify years of enjoyment or the effect of delay.
The warning not to fix one's gaze on benefits granted to others identifies bestowed plenty as a misleading object of attention.
The narrowly averted inclination is unrelated to the focus's extended provision and promised arrival.
Those who consumed their good things in worldly life face recompense, making enjoyment accountable and exhaustible.
The description of companions in Paradise does not illuminate the focus's earthly reprieve.
Seven years of cultivation concern prudent storage through a scheduled period, not enjoyment mistaken for security.
Joseph's additional years in prison add delayed time but no granted benefit or final warning.
This introductory report of what they say adds no relevant temporal or enjoyment element.
Seeing the promised matter as far off weakly parallels a delayed event, without addressing benefit during the wait.
Years of scarcity are an admonitory contrast to enjoyment, but do not explain its apparent extension.
The declaration that guidance belongs to Allah has no direct relation to prolonged enjoyment.
A life-course measured in years joins received blessing to gratitude and righteous action, offering an ethical response to extended life.
The challenge to wish for death concerns a claim about the hereafter, not years of granted enjoyment.
A day measured as fifty thousand years enlarges the temporal scale relevant to judging delay, without the benefit motif.
The description of enduring garden reward does not specifically clarify the focus's provisional worldly enjoyment.
Worldly enjoyment is called little and explicitly contrasted with the better hereafter, directly relativizing any extension of it.
Celestial measures make years and reckoning knowable, but this repeats the calendrical point without an enjoyment outcome.
A thousand-year measure for a divine day reinforces that human counting is not the scale of divine administration.
The unbeliever receives only brief enjoyment before being driven to the Fire, a direct individual analogue of the focus's warning.
Forty years of wandering are a measured disciplinary interval, not a case of enjoyment or presumed safety.
The settled refusal of disbelievers to heed warning supplies only a background for why reprieve may not reform.
Deliberate alteration after understanding concerns response to revelation, not the temporal logic of the focus.
The Lord lying in wait supplies an accountability horizon that prevents delay from implying neglect.
Earthly settlement and enjoyment until a time repeat the finite-worldly-use pattern, though less specifically than earlier cards.
Adam's teaching scene does not add to the focus's years, enjoyment, or consequence.
The pilgrimage technical use of tamattuʿ is unrelated to delayed worldly benefit.
The command concerning the cow does not illuminate the focus's temporal warning.
Rejection of confirming revelation parallels disbelief only generally and supplies no account of reprieve.
The reference is to lightning's brightness, not years; the lexical overlap gives no usable connection.
Reward for faith and righteous deeds provides only a broad contrast with worldly security inferred from enjoyment.
The command to worship sincerely supplies no relevant temporal or enjoyment element.
The mention of the tree of zaqqum signals punishment but adds no account of delayed benefit.
The believers' prayer for forgiveness does not clarify the focus's question about extended enjoyment.
Hidden motives exposed by a future divine act loosely resemble delayed disclosure, without the focus's benefit motif.
The inadequacy of conjecture for truth is not a substantive parallel to years of enjoyment.
Knowledge of unseen and seen grounds the larger judgment that makes an apparent reprieve intelligible.
Divine rather than human self-purification corrects self-assessment, but does not address delay or enjoyment.
Allah's knowledge of deeds underwrites justice and supplies an accountability frame against treating advantage as immunity.
The staged life course and appointed term give a broad model of bounded human duration and eventual resurrection.
Repentance and faith after wrongdoing show that a negative course can change before final judgment, a moral alternative within delay.
The extension granted to disbelievers is explicitly not for their good but for an increase in sin before humiliating punishment.
Worldly life is named deceptive enjoyment, directly rejecting permanence inferred from present benefit.
A little enjoyment is followed by Hell, making temporary use and final consequence explicit.
Abundant openings after forgetfulness end in sudden seizure at the height of their joy, closely matching delayed enjoyment overturned by arrival.
Worldly life as play and diversion supplies a broad contrast between transient use and the better hereafter.
Those deceived by worldly life are forgotten at judgment, linking present absorption to eventual reversal.
The enjoyment of worldly life is declared little beside the hereafter, directly relativizing its apparent abundance.
Wealth and children can be instruments of punishment in worldly life rather than signs of favor.
Earlier peoples' enjoyment of their allotted share becomes a warning against repeating their course.
Wealth and children are again denied evidentiary value because they can serve punishment rather than security.
Worldly enjoyment is followed by return to Allah and severe punishment for disbelief.
Those seeking worldly life and its adornment receive its full payment here but lose their share in the hereafter.
Joy in worldly life is contrasted with its being only enjoyment when set against the hereafter.
Preferring worldly life to the hereafter identifies the value inversion that makes extended benefit spiritually dangerous.
Allah defers people to an appointed term, showing that non-immediate judgment is a measured postponement.
Brief enjoyment is immediately paired with painful punishment.
Seeking the immediate is answered with a limited grant and then Hell, making worldly acquisition non-final.
The garden owner's cultivated wealth is destroyed, exposing worldly abundance as vulnerable rather than secure.
The parable of vegetation that becomes debris gives worldly flourishing a visibly passing form.
Wealth and children are only worldly adornment, while enduring good deeds are better in lasting value.
The splendor allotted to others in worldly life is explicitly a test, closely framing granted benefit as examination.
Good and evil are both tests and all return to Allah, providing the governing frame for a period of enjoyment.
The question directly challenges the assumption that extended wealth and children mean an acceleration of good for their recipients.
Many towns luxuriating in livelihood were destroyed, making prosperity no protection from eventual judgment.
What is given in worldly life is enjoyment and adornment, while what is with Allah is better and more enduring.
Worldly life is characterized as diversion and play against the reality of the final abode.
A community's abundant provision is followed by its turning away and receiving a consequential reversal.
Wealth and children are denied any power to bring people near to Allah, correcting an inference of favored status.
People are deferred to an appointed term, confirming that apparent non-punishment is not neglect.
Worldly life is explicitly called enjoyment, while the hereafter is the lasting home.
The world is described through material adornments that are only enjoyment of worldly life, reserved against the hereafter's value.
Taking Allah's signs in mockery and being deceived by worldly life leads to an irreversible final outcome.
Worldly life is play and diversion; faith and reverence redirect the value of what is possessed.
Wealth and children can distract from remembrance, identifying how continuing possession becomes spiritually costly.
Wealth and children are a trial, giving the focus's extended benefit an explicit testing function.
Those who deny are gradually drawn on from where they do not know, a direct pattern of hidden extension before reckoning.
Ample wealth, visible sons, and an eased path do not secure the recipient, who is instead threatened with a steep punishment.
Love of the immediate and neglect of the hereafter names the preference that makes temporal enjoyment deceptive.
Attachment to the immediate while leaving a grave day behind gives a moral diagnosis of present-oriented enjoyment.
Transgression joined to preferring worldly life ends in Hell, while restraint before the final standing has the Garden.
Preference for worldly life is corrected by the hereafter's being better and more enduring.
Human readings of expanded provision as honor and constricted provision as disgrace are explicitly rejected.
Rival accumulation distracts until the graves, showing worldly increase as a temporary preoccupation cut short by death.
Accumulated wealth is falsely imagined to make its owner immortal, directly exposing the illusion of lasting security.
